electric-cobalt.$description: Electric Cobalt — Primary action fills, active nav links, icon accents, link underlines. The only chromatic button color in the system — cobalt against the warm bone canvas makes every CTA feel switched on

ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Orange outline accent for tags, dividers, and focused UI edges. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

volt-lime.$description: Volt Lime — Promotional and urgency surfaces: top sale bar, Subscribe & Save tags, sale-bubble accents on product cards. Reads as a highlighter against the warm canvas — use sparingly, never as a section background

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Primary text, hairline borders, logo, icon strokes. The structural backbone — used aggressively for borders and dividers rather than reserving it for text alone

bone.$description: Bone — Page canvas and quiet section backgrounds. Warm off-white that gives the system its sunlit feel; never pure white at the page level

paper.$description: Paper — Elevated card surfaces, input fields, and any element that needs to sit forward of the bone canvas. Always a surface, never a text color

concrete.$description: Concrete — Soft borders, dividers, and secondary surface fills. Quieter than Obsidian when a hairline needs to recede

ash.$description: Ash — Muted helper text, secondary metadata, star-rating inactive state, and low-emphasis form labels

graphite.$description: Graphite — Slightly softened near-black for headings and dark UI surfaces where pure Obsidian feels too aggressive; button hover states on dark

mist.$description: Mist — Faint borders and disabled input outlines — one step lighter than Concrete for tertiary edges

pebble.$description: Pebble — Disabled button background, out-of-stock product card state. The only neutral allowed to function as an action fill, and only for disabled

founders-grotesk.$description: Primary typeface for body, headings, and product copy. Used across nearly every context — body, nav, hero, card, button, footer, heading. The geometric grotesque carries the brand voice: tight line-heights at large sizes (1.04–1.17 above 32px) make headlines feel like block letters slapped on the page rather than flowing paragraphs.

gt-planar.$description: Secondary typeface for fine print, sale tags, form labels, and dense UI metadata in the 10–14px range. A quieter geometric companion to Founders Grotesk — use it wherever a label needs to whisper instead of speak.

font-awesome-5-pro.$description: Font Awesome 5 Pro — detected in extracted data but not described by AI
